name: TX-36
label: Safe R

model.rationale: Babin is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by about twelve points, while Rhonda Hart has raised no money and no polls or expert ratings suggest a competitive race. Prediction markets give her roughly a six percent chance, consistent with a solid Republican hold.
model.watch: Any polling showing Hart within single digits or significant outside spending in the district would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Brian Babin seeks another term in this East Texas district, which leans Republican by about twelve points. He enters the general election with roughly $900,000 on hand after raising over $1 million, while Democratic challenger Rhonda Hart has reported no fundraising. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a six percent chance of an upset. The national environment may be favorable to Democrats, but with no money, no polling evidence of competitiveness, and a strong incumbent, the seat remains firmly in Republican hands. Babin is the clear favorite to win another term.
